strings.4858448: STEREO renders both eyes every frame. PERFORMANCE renders one eye per frame, in turn, and rebuilds the other: much faster at a very slight cost of quality in fast motion.
strings.4858624: The rendering resolution against what your VR runtime asks for. Higher is sharper, lower is faster. Takes effect after a restart.
strings.4858768: Renders the game at a lower resolution and upscales it, for more performance. FSR works on any GPU, DLSS on NVIDIA RTX cards.
strings.4858896: How low the upscaler renders. NATIVE AA keeps the full resolution and only smooths edges; the lower modes are faster but less sharp.
strings.4859040: Which DLSS model upscales. The DLSS 4.5 models look best but cost the most; AUTO uses K.
strings.4859136: Upscales only the middle of each eye's view, where you look, and keeps the edges simpler. Smaller angles are faster.
strings.4859264: How the edges outside FOVEATED UPSCALING's middle area are smoothed. NATIVE (FSR/FSR) is sharper but slower, TAA is faster and more blurry.
strings.4859408: What the desktop window shows while you play.
strings.4859456: The mirror also shows the HUD, menus and use prompts where the headset shows them, so it matches the headset exactly. For recording; slight performance cost.
strings.4859616: Renders the edges of your view in less detail, where you notice it least, for more performance. NVIDIA GPUs only.
strings.4859744: More accurate reflections on water, reaching further. Small performance penalty.
strings.4859840: Turns off the game's motion blur, which can be uncomfortable in VR.
strings.4859920: Controls game's Depth of Field which may look weird/blurry in VR. All bars is the game's own amount.
strings.4860032: How sharp the HUD and menus are. Higher is crisper and costs a little more. Takes effect after a restart.
strings.4860144: Gives the VR runtime the depth of each frame, so a late frame is shown steadier. Used only where the headset supports it.
strings.4860272: Which way pushing the move stick forward takes you: where you look, where your body faces, or where a controller points.
strings.4860400: HOLD crouches while the button is held. TOGGLE crouches with one press and stands up with the next.
strings.4860512: Sprint without a button: flick the move stick fully forward, let go, then push it fully forward again and hold to start sprinting.
strings.4860656: How far the move stick must be pushed before you move. Raise it if you drift with the stick untouched.
strings.4860768: How far the turn stick must be pushed before you turn. Raise it if you turn by accident.
strings.4860864: Tones down the game's camera bob while walking and running, which can be uncomfortable in VR.
strings.4860960: ROOM-SCALE lets you walk around your room. STANDING keeps you in one place. SEATED is for playing sitting down.
strings.4861072: Your real height, so the game can tell when you crouch. NOT SET uses the headset alone.
strings.4861168: How big the world looks. The game assets are built larger than in real life; 94% looks closest to real sizes.
strings.4861280: Crouching in real life crouches in the game. Needs PLAYER HEIGHT.
strings.4861360: Moves everything worn on the belt up or down: the holster, the magazine pouch, the gas mask, throwables, and the binoculars and charger on your back.
strings.4861520: STAY WITH YOU keeps the belt where your own is when you crouch. FOLLOW BODY moves it with the character's body. AUTO follows a real-life crouch only; set PLAYER HEIGHT for it (NOT SET: 178 CM).
strings.4861728: FOLLOW HEAD turns your body after your head once you look far enough to the side. LOCKED turns it only with the turn stick.
strings.4861856: FOLLOW lets you lean and step freely, the body walking after you. LOCKED keeps your view over the body, and real steps move the body along.
strings.4862000: Experimental: enables support for bHaptics. Requires the bHaptics Player to be installed. You feel shots, hits, explosions, the heartbeat, landings and steps.
strings.4862160: Tilts weapons and items in your hand up or down, to match how you hold your controller.
strings.4862256: Your fingers follow your real ones where the controllers sense them. Off, they follow the trigger, grip and buttons.
strings.4862384: HOLD keeps what you take while the grip is held. TOGGLE takes it with one grip and puts it back with a grip where it was taken.
strings.4862512: With nothing in your hand's reach, the use button uses what you look at, as in the flat game. Helps with things a hand cannot reach.
strings.4862656: How strongly the controllers vibrate. 50% is as the game made it, 100% twice that; 0% turns all vibration off.
strings.4862768: Light ticks as your hand reaches a body slot, something to take, a weapon part or a device.
strings.4862864: The kick of every shot in the hands holding the gun, and the weapons' own vibration.
strings.4862952: Vibration when you are hit or hurt.
strings.4862992: Vibration in scripted scenes and while riding vehicles.
strings.4863048: Light steps while running, and landings.
